# Subtopology Decomposition

Each subsystem is assembled as an F' subtopology containing its application, hardware managers, and driver connections. The diagrams below are the current high-level topology views. Detailed FPP instances, ports, and connections remain subject to the corresponding subsystem designs.

## Sensing and Science Subtopologies

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    subgraph ADCS["ADCS Subtopology"]
        direction TB
        AdcsApp["AdcsApplication"]
        Immu["ImmuManager"]
        SunSensor["SunSensorManager"]
        Mtq["MagnetorquerManager"]
        AdcsApp --> Immu
        AdcsApp --> SunSensor
        AdcsApp --> Mtq
    end

    subgraph DC["DataCollection Subtopology"]
        direction TB
        DCApp["DataCollectionApplication"]
        Cam1["LOST camera manager"]
        Cam2["FOUND camera manager"]
        DCApp --> Cam1
        DCApp --> Cam2
    end

    subgraph SI["Science Inference"]
        direction TB
        SIApp["ScienceInferenceApplication"]
    end

    ADCS ~~~ DC
    DC ~~~ SI
```

The two camera managers are the software owners for the USB-connected LOST and FOUND cameras. SCOPE uses both cameras during calibration experiments.

## Power and Communications Subtopologies

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    subgraph COMMS["Comms Subtopology"]
        direction TB
        CommsApp["ComApplication"]
        TRM["TmtcRadioManager"]
        CommsApp --> TRM
    end

    subgraph EPSSUB["EPS Subtopology"]
        direction TB
        EPSApp["EPSApplication"]
        Mppt["MpptManager"]
        Curr["CurrentSensorManager"]
        Watchdog["WatchdogPinger"]
        Deploy["DeployPanelsManager"]
        Mppt --> EPSApp
        Curr --> EPSApp
        EPSApp --> Deploy
    end

    subgraph THERM["Thermal Subtopology"]
        direction TB
        ThermApp["ThermalApplication"]
        TempSensor["TemperatureSensorManager"]
        Heater["HeaterManager"]
        ThermApp --> TempSensor
        ThermApp --> Heater
    end

    COMMS ~~~ EPSSUB
    EPSSUB ~~~ THERM
```

`WatchdogPinger` is scheduled by the EPS rate-group path and directly services the EPS hardware watchdog. The radio manager is shared with the communications framing services at the top-level topology.

## Shared Infrastructure and Framework Services

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    subgraph SYS["Level 4 - Shared System Services"]
        direction TB
        Cmd["Svc::CmdDispatcher"]
        Events["Svc::EventManager"]
        Health["Svc::Health"]
        Fatal["Svc::FatalHandler"]
        Cmd --> Events
        Events --> Fatal
    end

    subgraph CCSDS["ComCcsds (F' provided)"]
        direction TB
        ComQueue["Svc::ComQueue and framing chain"]
    end

    subgraph FH["FileHandling (F' provided)"]
        direction TB
        FileIO["Svc::FileUplink / Svc::FileDownlink / Svc::FileManager"]
    end

    subgraph DP["DataProducts (F' provided)"]
        direction TB
        Dp["Svc::DpManager / Svc::DpWriter / Svc::DpCatalog"]
    end

    SYS ~~~ CCSDS
    CCSDS ~~~ FH
    FH ~~~ DP
```

These are framework services and reusable subtopology groupings, not additional mission-specific hardware-manager layers. Their individual component responsibilities are documented in the Level 3 and Level 4 sections according to whether they are application-facing data-path services or deployment-wide services.

## Satellite-Mode Command Fan-Out

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    SSM["SatStateMachine<br/>(Level 4)"]
    subgraph APPS["Application Layer"]
        direction TB
        AdcsApp["AdcsApplication"]
        DCApp["DataCollectionApplication"]
        SIApp["ScienceInferenceApplication"]
        CommsApp["ComApplication"]
        ThermApp["ThermalApplication"]
        AdcsApp ~~~ DCApp
        DCApp ~~~ SIApp
        SIApp ~~~ CommsApp
        CommsApp ~~~ ThermApp
    end
    SSM --> AdcsApp
    SSM --> DCApp
    SSM --> SIApp
    SSM --> CommsApp
    SSM --> ThermApp
```

The state machine sends each application its own typed mode enum. Applications do not need to understand the satellite-wide state or communicate directly with the Level 4 mode coordinator beyond that interface.
